title: Chinese knotting
summary: Chinese knotting ties a single length of cord, usually red silk, into symmetrical flat knots such as the button, cloverleaf, double coin and pan chang. Pieces are hung as ornaments or used as fasteners and tassels on clothing.
howToPlay: The framed picture shows the finished knot: one red cord, with a tassel.
Gold rings mark the crossings the cord must make. Tap or drag from point to point to lay the cord; where it crosses itself it passes over, then under, and the gaps are drawn for you.
Pass straight through every ring twice, once across and once up and down.
Tap the first point to close the cord into a loop, then press Check.
rules: The cord is one piece: no stretch between two points is used twice.
A crossing counts when the cord passes straight through that point twice.
Three stars need every marked crossing made and the cord closed into a loop.
heritageNote: Cord knotting in China goes back to antiquity and spread as clothing decoration under the Tang and Song dynasties, becoming a household art under the Qing. Knotters work in silk or cotton cord, mostly red, often adding beads, jade or a tassel.
